comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C23-C31. Both evaluations find the immunofluorescence, in situ hybridization, and spatial expression data SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative imaging and correlation with EMT, while peer reviewers accept these as foundational descriptive findings providing context for mechanistic claims.

Perfect agreement on claims C35-C43. Both evaluations find the blood flow manipulation experiments SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights reversibility and tissue-specific responses, while peer reviewers specifically praise the experimental approach and controls as 'convincing' strengths.

Perfect agreement on claims C44-C47. Both evaluations find the hypoxia controls and orthogonal flow-reduction methods SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes convergence of multiple methods, while peer reviewers specifically commend the care taken to minimize confounding effects of hypoxia.

Perfect agreement on claims C48-C56. Both evaluations find the mTORC2-PKC-Notch signaling pathway SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights pharmacological, genetic, and rescue experiments, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm this as a novel mechanotransduction pathway with 'largely convincing' data.

Perfect agreement on claims C66-C68. Both evaluations find the pharmacogenetic interaction data SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance and use of multiple drugs, while peer reviewers accept these data as demonstrating clinical relevance without challenge.

Agreement on claims C57-C63 being SUPPORTED, with OpenEval finding all claims C57-C65 supported while peer review only explicitly addresses C57-C63. Both accept caveolin-1 redistribution and SEM data. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative caveolae measurements, while peer reviewers highlight novel insights on caveolin-1 localization and imaging quality.

Disagreement on claims C64-C65 (cholesterol rescue mechanism). OpenEval finds these claims SUPPORTED as part of R6, establishing causal link between membrane lipid structure and signaling. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 stating 'more evidence will be needed' and questioning how general cholesterol addition produces regionalized effects.

Partial overlap on claims C33-C34 (Dll4 knockout data). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to confounding vascular dysfunction, while peer reviewers find these claims SUPPORTED as part of the ligand-independent mechanism (also including C2-C3). Peer reviewers describe the Dll4 knockout data as 'convincingly support[ing]' ligand-independence, while OpenEval expresses caution about interpretation.

Partial overlap on claims C2-C3 (central conclusions about ligand-independent Notch activation). Both evaluations find these SUPPORTED. OpenEval groups these with C4 as summary claims integrating all experimental evidence, while peer reviewers group with C33-C34 (Dll4 data) as core findings affirmed by all three reviewers.

Substantial overlap on claims C1, C5-C19 (literature context). Both evaluations find these SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes these as established knowledge providing foundation for novel findings, while peer reviewers accept them as contextual claims that are well-established and not questioned.

Substantial overlap on claims C20-C22, C69-C82 (discussion and literature context). Both evaluations find these SUPPORTED. OpenEval characterizes them as secondary supporting information for interpreting findings, while peer reviewers accept them as part of the established developmental framework without challenge.

Minimal overlap on claim C4 (membrane lipid microstructure hypothesis). OpenEval finds C4 SUPPORTED as part of R9 (central conclusions), while peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN in R7, stating the hypothesis is 'fascinating' but requires 'more evidence' to prove the mechanistic link between membrane structure and signaling.
